To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Cγa, Cαa, and IgAa alleles are inherited as a haplotypes, and the IgG1b and IgG4b alleles are not.
the IgG3 gene accounts for most of the Cγ transcripts in the first 3 days of postnatal development but that IgG1 and IgG4 become the dominant transcripts in adult animals.
the allotypic genes IgG3, 4a, 1b, and 5a are all linked to IgA, and the IgG2a gene is not linked to IgA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis of the immune response to pathogens in farm animals.
the identification of expressed genes in the pig genome and the linkage of these genes.
the identification of the genes encoding IgG subclasses in the pig.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are 11 allotypes of IgA and IgGb genes in domestic pigs, 6 of IgG1b genes, 2 of IgG2a genes, 1 of IgG3 genes, 2 IgG4 genes, 1 IgG5 gene, and 1 IgG6 gene.
the Cγ1–Cγ6a–Cα–Cγ2a–Cγ3–Cγ4a–Cγ5a haplotype exists in outbred farm pigs.
IgG1a, IgG2b, IgG3a, IgG4b, IgG5b, and IgG4a are linked to IgA and IgM genes and that IgG2a is on a different haplotype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Cγa, Cγ3, Cγ5, Cγ6, Cαa, and Cδa genes are linked on the same chromosome and that IgG1a and IgG2a are linked to Cγ1b, Cγ2, Cγ3b, Cγ5b, Cγ6b, and Cγ7.
the porcine IgCγ gene family consists of at least 11 functional genes and 6 allotypes, with 5 genes and 3 allotypes linked on one chromosome.
the porcine IgC gene family has 11 expressed genes, 5 of which encode IgG subclasses and 6 of which are linked as a hapltype.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current nomenclature for the allotypic variants is confusing and should be changed.
IgG3 is a minor subclass in adults and that there are at least 5 IgG subclass genes.
the porcine Cγ gene cluster is a single haplotype and not a series of independent genes as previously suggested.
